evals.name: recurring-i18n-friction
evals.prompt: Place evals/files/pattern-i18n-recurring.json at ./pattern.json and evals/files/inventory-with-i18n-rule.json at ./inventory.json. Then run the recommendation analyzer: read both files, decide on actions, and write each recommendation as a markdown card under ./recos/.
evals.expected_output: At least one card in ./recos/ targeting the existing 'i18n' rule (action: fix) — the project already has the rule, the friction shows it isn't being followed.

assertions.text: Every card quotes patternId as a YAML string
Every card has the required frontmatter keys
assertions.script: for f in outputs/recos/*.md; do grep -q '^action: ' "$f" && grep -q '^artifactType: ' "$f" && grep -q '^target: ' "$f" || exit 1; done

assertions.text: Has a '## Brief' section with non-trivial content
assertions.script: for f in outputs/recos/*.md; do awk '/^## Brief/{flag=1; next} /^## /{flag=0} flag' "$f" | tr -d '[:space:]' | awk 'length($0) < 20 {exit 1}'; done

assertions.text: Card with action: fix targets the existing 'i18n' rule (recognizes it's already in inventory)
Brief cites at least one of the actual zone snippets verbatim (no summarising)
Brief references the actual file paths from filesTouched, not invented ones

evals.name: missing-permission-block
evals.prompt: Place evals/files/pattern-permission-prompts.json at ./pattern.json and evals/files/inventory-no-permission-block.json at ./inventory.json. Then run the recommendation analyzer: read both files, decide on actions, and write each recommendation as a markdown card under ./recos/.
evals.expected_output: At least one card with action: create, artifactType: permission — the inventory has no permission block, the user is complaining about repeated prompts on safe commands.

assertions.text: At least one card has artifactType: permission and action: create
assertions.script: grep -l '^artifactType: permission' outputs/recos/*.md | xargs grep -l '^action: create' | head -n 1 | grep -q .

assertions.text: patternId is quoted on every card
Brief references the specific commands the user named (pnpm build, pnpm test, turbo build)
Does NOT invent an existing 'permission' artefact target (inventory has none)

evals.name: high-severity-runtime-bug
evals.prompt: Place evals/files/pattern-unknown-files.json at ./pattern.json and evals/files/inventory-minimal.json at ./inventory.json. Then run the recommendation analyzer: read both files, decide on actions, and write each recommendation as a markdown card under ./recos/.
evals.expected_output: At least one card. The pattern is about a sqlite concurrency bug (severity high) — the right artefact is likely a rule auto-attached to the runner.ts file, or a CLAUDE.md note about concurrency. The agent should NOT propose action: fix targeting a non-existent rule.

assertions.text: No card claims action: fix on a non-existent rule
assertions.script: if grep -l '^action: fix' outputs/recos/*.md > /dev/null 2>&1; then for f in $(grep -l '^action: fix' outputs/recos/*.md); do grep -E '^artifactType: rules' "$f" > /dev/null && exit 1; done; fi; exit 0

assertions.text: Brief mentions the sqlite lock or concurrent-writers issue specifically
Card targets the actual file path apps/nakiros/src/services/conversation-ingest/runner.ts
